q2.answer: In the bone of the gum, next to the front teeth. It is called the alveolar cleft.

q3.answer: The small tooth next to the front tooth (lateral incisor) is missing. About half of children with a cleft do not have it on the cleft side.

q4.answer: The eye tooth needs bone to grow down into. The graft gives it bone to come down into.
q4.where: Sheet 1, The eye tooth and Why surgeons do the bone graft

q5.answer: About 8 to 11 years old. They go by how far the teeth have grown, not age.
q5.where: Sheet 1, When surgeons do the graft

q7.answer: New bone fills the gap and the gum has healed over it. The eye tooth is a little lower than before.
q7.where: Sheet 2, key message box and What has changed

q8.answer: With an X-ray at about 3 to 6 months. It shows how well the new bone has taken.

q9.answer: Your hip can be sore for a while after.

q10.answer: It has come down through the new bone and is in the row of teeth.

q12.answer: Two plans. One is close the space: braces move the eye tooth into the gap and the dentist reshapes it to look like the missing tooth. The other is keep the space: a plate with a false tooth while you grow, then later an implant or a bridge. Your cleft team will talk with you about which suits you.
